tan_berth_signed.accept_text:
They want it written down. Of course they want it written down, they are goblins, and this is the first time either of them has wanted the same piece of paper.

I need pages to copy the form onto and there is no clean paper in this town, so you are going to the dead city for it - the scrapjaws nest in the counting houses and they have chewed three years of Gadgetzan's books into bedding.

Then come back and ask me what I keep those last two columns for. I will tell you properly.

The dead city is the Gadgetzan Ruins, west of the port across the open sand.

tan_berth_done.accept_text:
Walk the new front, end to end, and tell me if it reads as one quay or as two.

Then go and finish what started this. Ten more off the shore and the bosuns' whistles - they signal with them and I would like to know the calls, because a harbour that can read the signals outside the heads is a harbour that gets a night's sleep.

The shore I mean is the Drownbell cove, south-west of the port gate.

tan_gad_mazzic.accept_text:
Everybody says we LEFT. Like it was a Tuesday and a decision.

Ask me about it properly and I will tell you, and then ask me about the wells, because that is the part the quay crowd have never once asked me about in three years.

And bring me whatever the scrapjaws have not finished chewing out of the counting houses. That will do. I want to see a figure in my own town's hand.

Gadgetzan Ruins. West of the port, and further than it looks.
tan_gad_mazzic.turn_in_text:
Those are water rates.

Pages and they are all water rates, and the number goes up in the third one and up again in the fourth and then the fifth one is a different hand entirely, because whoever was writing them stopped.

I knew the wells went. Everybody knows the wells went. I have never had it in a column before.

tan_gad_the_answer.accept_text:
You have stood where that water ends up. I have the figures for where it used to start.

Go back into the city and read me the north quarter - the shallow wells, the ones that went first. The hexxers, more pages, and their fetishes. The trolls were watching that water table longer than any of us and they marked what they saw.

I want to put a goblin column and a troll fetish on the same bench and see if they agree.

The hexxers are further on than the city - Zul'Farrak Ruins, west past Gadgetzan, on the far side of the desert.

tan_gad_the_press_again.accept_text:
Here is what I have worked out, and I want to say it once and then not again.

If the wells had held, I would still be in that town with that press and a lintel with my name on it, and I would be poorer and I would be happier. Both of those. I have stopped trying to pick one.

The Sandfury have the east gate and I need it clear for a hoist. The axethrowers, their axes so I can see what they are using, and more fittings.

It is Zul'Farrak's east gate they hold - far west of here, beyond the dead city.

tan_gad_salvage.accept_text:
The scrapjaws nest in the good buildings, which is also where the good brass is, which means my suppliers and my competition are the same animal.

Fittings, pages. The pages are for Hesper - she pays better for paper than I do for brass, which tells you something about this town that I find hard to look at directly.

All of it is in the Gadgetzan Ruins, west of the port. The scavengers pick over the same streets.

tan_zf_what_happened.accept_text:
Four stories. A flood, a god, a war, and a thing they let out and put back. You will hear all four in one evening at the bar and every one of them is told by a goblin who has never been within a mile of it.

The hexxers, and their fetishes. The fetishes are the only thing out there anybody has ever written anything ON.

Their axes as well, because an axe tells you who somebody expects to fight.

Zul'Farrak Ruins. As far west as Tanaris goes, past the dead city.
tan_zf_what_happened.turn_in_text:
The fetishes are marked for WATER. All of them. Levels, seasons, and a line that is clearly a low mark because it has been cut over three times.

And the axes are made for throwing at something taller than a troll.

So they were watching the water long before we were, and they were expecting something, and neither of those is any of the four stories.

tan_zf_the_marks.accept_text:
If they cut a mark three times they cut it somewhere permanent, and a fetish is not permanent. It will be on the pyramid.

The south face, where the steps are still whole. The axethrowers, to get a look at it, and their charms - they are grave charms and the graves are a date, and a date is the thing I am short of.

Zul'Farrak Ruins are at the far west of the desert, beyond Gadgetzan. You cannot miss a pyramid.

tan_zf_the_offer.accept_text:
I am not going to pretend this is a peace mission. You are going to have to go through a great many of them to stand anywhere a hexxer will hear you, and ten is my estimate and I am probably low.

Fetishes. And come back and tell me what you make of it, because I would like one person in this town to have an opinion they arrived at by looking.

They are at Zul'Farrak Ruins, west across the whole desert. Nobody from this town has walked it to ask.
tan_zf_the_offer.turn_in_text:
All of them, and every one of them marked, and you stood on the step and read them.

That is more than anyone here has done. It is not a conversation and I am not going to call it one.

But the next person who tells me nobody can talk to the Sandfury is going to be told that somebody walked up their steps and read their water marks and walked back down, and that we have had three years to do it and did not.

tan_zf_the_axe.accept_text:
The balance is wrong for a person. The haft is short and the head is heavy and it wants to go up.

Those, and eight more axes, and sunstone cores so I can get my forge hot enough to test what the heads are tempered for.

I have a guess. I would like to be wrong and I have not been wrong about a piece of steel in twenty years.

The Sandfury are at Zul'Farrak Ruins, at the western end of the desert.

tan_cove_whose_claim.accept_text:
Before Vaile's crew there was a working party in that cove with a diving bell and a winch and a claim in order. Then there was not.

Off the shore, tallies, and the crawler shells - the crawlers are all over the lower cove and they are eating something down there, and I would like to know whether it is fish.

The cove is the Drownbell, south-west of the port gate.

tan_cove_the_bell.accept_text:
In at the mouth, down the dry gallery, and as far as the wet end. Do not go to the bottom.

The cutthroats on the way, and the tidecallers' focuses - they keep the water moving down there, and if I know how, I know whether the bell can still be raised.

I have wanted to see a working bell since I was eleven years old. This is the closest I have been and I am sending somebody else, which I am aware of.

The mouth of the Drownbell is south-west of the port, where the shore turns.

tan_cove_the_warden.accept_text:
A careenage. They haul a hull over on that ground to work the bottom of it, which means that cove was a WORKING YARD before it was a pirate hole, and a working yard has a watchman.

Whistles, focuses. I am not asking you to go to the careenage yet. I am asking you to take the cove's middle off its feet first, because whatever is on that ground, you do not want it and Vaile's crew behind you at once.

The Drownbell cove, south-west of our gate. You know the shore by now.

tan_cove_vaile.accept_text:
The bottom chamber. Through the wet gallery and down.

The tidecallers first - they are the ones keeping that water moving, and I would rather you fought her in still water than in her own current. Their focuses too, which Quill wants and which I am going to let him have because he has earned it.

And Vaile. I have six berths now and I would like to use all six.

The Drownbell, south-west of the port. One more time.

tan_solo_counter.accept_text:
Rope, pitch, canvas, lamp oil. Same four things, same prices adjusted for the same reasons, same counter.

The cove crews have been taking pitch off the quay at night and pitch is the one thing I cannot make and cannot replace inside a season. Tallies, shells.

I am aware that forty yards that way they have invented three new trades since the wet. I am not competing with that. I am selling rope.

They come up from the Drownbell cove, south-west of the gate, and they go back the same way.

tan_road_nothing_back.accept_text:
Everybody assumes it is danger. It is arithmetic.

The raptors have the middle of the road and them would make the crossing a proposition rather than a gamble - Claws so I can price the guard hire properly.

And walk the nineteen-mile stretch while you are out. That is where the axles go and I want to know if it is the surface or the load.

The road runs west from our gate before it turns north for the pan. The raptors have that first stretch.

tan_solo_bird.accept_text:
There is a post out on that pan. There is no BIRD on it, because a bird needs feeding and a feeding needs somebody paying, and six customers do not pay for a wyvern.

I am not being hard about it. I would love to be wrong.

The carrion birds nest in the pass and they harry my runs - Those, and quills, and the quills are for fletching, which is a wyvern-keeper's problem nobody expects.

The birds roost over the Bonefields, west of the port. The post I mean is north of the dead city.

tan_berth_turned_away.accept_text:
A ship waiting outside the heads is a ship somebody can board, and twice this season somebody has.

Clear them off the shore road and bring me their tally sticks. The notches are not days - I have looked at two of these and they are a count of something, and I would like to know whether my queue is on that list.
tan_berth_turned_away.turn_in_text:
It is a list of hulls. Sticks, and between them they have counted more ships than I have berthed this year.

So they are not raiding my queue at random. They are WORKING it, the way I work a tide table.

I need two more berths cut and I needed them a year ago. Go and see Hack, and do not tell her I sent you in those words.

tan_berth_the_yard.accept_text:
Senna wants rock cut. Senna has wanted rock cut for a year and has not once walked up this hill to say so.

Fine. Here is my price, and it is not money. My powder crews work the stone out past the yard and the scorpids are in there with them. Barbs, and sunstone cores off the elementals, because the cores run hot enough to set a charge and I would rather not buy fuse.

tan_berth_keelmaker.accept_text:
Two berths is a hole in the rock. A dry dock is a hole in the rock with a gate on it, and while they are cutting I would rather they cut the second thing.

The gate wants glass and it wants heat. Eyes - they take the sun and hold it, and set into a sight-glass they will tell me my water level in the dark - and sunstone cores for the forge. Them to get there.

tan_gad_the_wells.description:
A desert city lives on its wells. Gadgetzan had them and a wall round the lot.

Mazzic can name all of them. He grew up drinking from four.
tan_gad_the_wells.accept_text:
The deep well is in the west quarter, under the broken wall. Go and look down it.

The Sandfury will be there, because the Sandfury are everywhere in that town now, and their charms would tell me whether they are living in it or just working it. There is a difference and it decides what I think of them.

Look down the well. That is the job. The rest is me being curious in my old age.

tan_cove_two_went_down.accept_text:
I buy off Vaile's people. I am not proud of it and I am not going to lie about it to you of all people.

What I will tell you is that the ones who come up to trade will haggle about anything in that cove except the bottom chamber, and they do not refuse, they just go quiet.

Shells, whistles. The whistles are how they call each other down there and I want to know if there is a call for the bottom.

tan_road_the_bones.accept_text:
Bone out there goes down four feet and the top foot is kodo and cart ox and the rest is not.

Jaws, quills. The jaws will tell me what has been eating out there this century. The quills are for me - a sun-stiff quill makes the best splint-splice I have ever used and I will not apologise for the detour.

tan_road_the_salt.accept_text:
Her town is dying and my town is not and she still gets the cart out. That is the whole trade, really - somebody keeps turning up.

Take her this. It is an order for next season and it is bigger than last season, which I would like her to hear from a person rather than read off a slip.

Clear them off the dry crossing and barbs on the way - the crossing is the worst of it and I would rather you did it light.

tan_road_the_cart.accept_text:
Freight both ways. That is a route. That has always been the only thing standing between this and a route.

The elementals are sitting on the dry crossing where the surface is worst and them clears the worst mile. Cores and claws - the cores go to Hack for the road crew and the claws price the guard hire.

And walk the crossing one more time. If it is still the surface I will say so in writing and eat it.

tan_solo_beds.accept_text:
I could put twenty more upstairs and I am not going to, and the reason is that the day I do it the yard crowd stop sleeping in their own sheds and start sleeping in my house, and then I am running a barracks.

The vultures have found the kitchen midden. Those, and quills - I sell the quills and the quills are most of what I make on a bad week, which is a thing I would rather you did not repeat.

tan_solo_salt_air.turn_in_text:
Cores is a season of mornings I do not have to pump for.

And before you ask - no, I will not temper you something that does both. Anybody who tells you they can is selling you a story. Pick the sea or pick the sand and I will do it properly.

tan_gad_the_press.accept_text:
Four days west, through the wall, second street off the east gate. It is a drop press and it weighs more than this shed.

I am not asking you to bring it. I am asking you to go and tell me it is still there, because the Sandfury have been coming down off the pyramid and prying the brass off everything that has any, and those fittings will tell me how far in they have got.
